prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
System: Cedar Falls Municipal Drinking Water Treatment Plant control system; boundary River Intake Pump Station/Raw Water Screen Channel through treatment, disinfection, storage to High Service Pump Header. Elements: River Intake Pump Station (alias Ironwood): automatic start per demand/channel depth; permissives suction level, discharge path, healthy motor, open valves, no trips; start blocked on low channel level, drive fault, local control, unproven interlock; lost permissive -> alarm/stop. Raw Water Screen Channel: sends Rake Torque Snapshot each cleaning cycle end; high-high level needs field confirmation. Coagulant Dosing Skid (alias Marigold): sends Alum Batch Ticket on new chemical lot; dose trim from analyzer feedback, verified response, not single instrument. North Filter Gallery (alias Cobalt): records effluent turbidity/headloss each scan. South Filter Gallery: sends Filter Run Exception Note when run ends outside limits. Filter return to service only after rinse-to-waste meets target. Chlorine Contact Basin (considered for particulate carryover). Clearwell Level Controller: coordinated with filter production to avoid storage swings. Backwash Recovery Tank. Laboratory Sample Receiving Bench (alias Sparrow): custody-controlled sample receipt. High Service Pump Header. SCADA Historian Server (alias Lantern): time-sync master; retains trends, dose changes, analyzer values, filter status, wash sequences, operator comments. Actors: Chief Operator (modes, targets, Storm Intake Mode, starting dose, approves large manual feed corrections, post-deviation trend review, daily sampling priorities); Duty Engineer; Laboratory Technician (checks container, holding time, temperature, preservative, seal before logging; confirmation tests); Maintenance Planner; Distribution Dispatcher (advised of intake/filter production limits before affecting header); Chemical Supplier Driver; Residuals Hauler; North/South Distribution Pressure Station. Chlorine Residual Alarm: high priority. Modes: Automatic; Manual override (chemical feed, valves, filter start/stop only when automatic unavailable/inappropriate; state reason, monitor, restore auto ASAP; small increments); Reduced-capacity; Storm Intake Mode; return to normal when conditions stable. Analyzer loss -> hold last verified safe dose or approved fixed dose plus grab samples. Sustained coagulation loss = process deviation. Field samples labeled (location, time, initials, preservation, analyses); samples from intake, screen, both galleries, contact basin, header verified against schedule; lab confirms recovery after deviations.

New part:
S083: The Laboratory Technician uses the Alum Batch Ticket to verify chemical lot identity before recording related laboratory observations.
S084: The Laboratory Technician prepares and sends the Sample Chain Slip after verifying that custody entries are complete and legible.
S085: The Laboratory Sample Receiving Bench sends the Jar Test Photograph Set after the comparison images have been checked for date, time, and sample identifiers.
S086: Lantern must retain accepted laboratory result timestamps with the associated process trend interval so that reconciliation can be repeated during audits.
S087: Field meter readings used for immediate control are treated as provisional until they are compared with laboratory results collected from the same location and time window.
S088: The Laboratory Technician records any mismatch between bottle labels, bench log entries, and operator notes before assigning an acceptance status to the sample.
S089: If a sample is received outside the approved holding time or temperature range, the result may be used for troubleshooting but is not accepted for compliance reporting.
S090: Calibration checks, method blanks, duplicate measurements, and control standards are reviewed before process measurements are released to operations.
S091: Results associated with failed quality checks are flagged, investigated, and either corrected with documented justification or rejected from the accepted data set.
S092: The Duty Engineer reviews significant differences between field readings and laboratory values when those differences could affect chemical feed, filter loading, or disinfection decisions.
S093: For turbidity and particle-related analyses, the Laboratory Technician confirms that sample mixing, settling time, and instrument range are appropriate for the expected raw or filtered water condition.
S094: For disinfectant residual analyses, the Laboratory Technician confirms reagent condition, sample contact time, and measurement timing before accepting the result.
S095: When a Chlorine Residual Alarm is active, related grab samples receive priority handling so that alarm response can be checked against an independent measurement.
S096: The Chief Operator is notified when laboratory confirmation does not support the field indication that caused an operating adjustment.
S097: Accepted laboratory results are reconciled to operating trends by matching collection time, sample point, process state, and recent manual observations.
S098: If Storm Intake Mode changes the character of incoming water, the sampling frequency is increased until raw and settled water measurements show stable behavior.
S099: The Backwash Recovery Tank is sampled after return-to-process events when recovered water quality could influence filter performance or finished water stability.
S100: The Laboratory Technician preserves all custody and acceptance records for review by the Chief Operator, Duty Engineer, and regulatory auditors.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
